tags.description: SS Inchulva, a 386-foot British steamship (built 1892 as Alberta), grounded in the September 11, 1903 hurricane about 150 yards off Delray Beach in roughly 15-25 feet of water; nine crew died. Shore-accessible; boilers and a debris field are the main visible features. Sources disagree on crew size (27 vs 28) and on whether the hull broke into three or five pieces.
tags.name: S.S. Inchulva / Delray Wreck
Julia Tuttle Causeway Artificial Reef
tags.description: Multi-deployment Miami-Dade artificial reef site in Biscayne Bay: about 727 tons of limerock boulders placed April 18, 2019 on the previously deployed Larson Barge (32 ft, 17 ft relief), plus later concrete, piling and boulder deployments in 23-32 ft. Construction records only; no dive reports found.
tags.qa_note: 2026-10-02 re-audit: only 2 independent domains (county + contractor) confirmed; floridadep.gov source removed because it does not mention the reef; no dive-operator source found. Marine life unsourced.

tags.name: Lofthus
tags.description: Iron barque Lofthus (ex-Cashmere, built Sunderland 1868, 222 ft, 1,277 GRT) wrecked February 4, 1898 off Manalapan; 16 crew survived. Scattered remains about 290 x 50 ft in 15-20 ft of water, up to ~6 ft relief; Florida Underwater Archaeological Preserve, NRHP 2004. Sources conflict on how the crew reached shore and on cargo volume.

British steel steamship Copenhagen (built 1898 Sunderland, 325 ft, 3,297 GRT per Wikipedia) wrecked in 1900 on the Pompano Dropoff off Lauderdale-by-the-Sea carrying coal to Havana. Florida Underwater Archaeological Preserve #5 and NRHP-listed. Sources conflict on exact date (May 20 vs 26), depth (12-39 ft depending on source) and who was responsible for the navigation error.
tags.name: SS Copenhagen Shipwreck

tags.description: Shore-accessible nearshore reef lines just south of Anglin's Fishing Pier, entered from the Datura Avenue beach portal; reefs lie roughly 100-400 ft from the beach at about 8-20 ft. South Florida Diving Headquarters separately lists a boat-dived 'Anglin Pier Reef' at 50-60 ft. The pier structure has been closed since November 2022 storm damage.
tags.name: Anglins Pier Reef

tags.description: Shallow shore dive at Phil Foster Park in Lake Worth Lagoon, best at high slack tide, depth about 15-25 ft; widely known for seahorses, frogfish, octopus, batfish and nudibranchs. Includes an 800-ft snorkel trail with limestone boulders and reef modules. Dive flag required; avoid the boat channel.

North-south limestone ledge reef offshore from the Breakers Hotel at Palm Beach in 50-65 ft; ledge 5-10 ft high on the west side. Gulf Stream drift dive for Open Water divers; turtles reported in spring and summer.

Artificial reef of decommissioned Gulf of Mexico oil platforms placed October 1985 off Hallandale Beach/Fort Lauderdale. Top decks of the recreational platforms at about 60, 80 and 100 ft; deepest platforms around 200 ft. Sources disagree on whether three or five rigs were donated. Some platforms lean about 45 degrees after Hurricane Andrew (1992).

Dataset entry for the reef area off Haulover Inlet (boat dive). No source consulted lists a site by this exact name; neighboring documented sites include Pete's Reef (~42 ft), Rock Pile (~30 ft) and Deep Trench (48-60 ft).
tags.qa_note: 2026-10-02 re-audit: no source found for a dive site named 'Haulover Ledge'; description limited to neighboring named sites. Needs a source or renaming.

tags.description: Atlantis-themed underwater memorial and artificial reef 3.25 miles east of Key Biscayne in about 40-45 ft of water, boat access only. Reported marine life includes barracuda, southern stingrays, green moray eels, spiny lobsters and long-spined sea urchins.

Rapa Nui Reef: a 150-ft barge that flipped when sunk on June 7, 2015 off Deerfield Beach and crushed most of its Moai-style sculptures; lies inverted in about 67 ft, rising 9 ft. Anchor or drift dive in 50-70 ft.

Datura Avenue beach portal in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea: shore entry to nearshore reef lines about 100-400 ft out at roughly 8-20 ft, plus the 2002 Shipwreck Snorkel Trail in about 10 ft. Tank rack on the beach, metered parking.

name: Jupiter Wreck Trek (Zion Train / Miss Jenny / Esso Bonaire)

tags.notes: Three-wreck drift site off Jupiter: Zion Train (164 ft Dutch-built freighter, scuttled June 2003, broken up by 2004 hurricanes), Miss Jenny (inverted barge) and Esso Bonaire (146 ft, sunk 1980s, upright), in roughly 80-90 ft. Goliath grouper aggregation Aug-Sep (counts vary widely by source); lemon sharks Jan-Feb.

Multi-mile limestone ledge off Juno Beach/Jupiter. Reported depths about 65-93 ft (one forum report to ~130 ft); ledge height reported as 6-15 ft or about 20 ft depending on source. Boat drift dive; lemon sharks reported, with winter aggregations of 50+ (Dec-Mar) per one source.

Dutch-built freighter (1970, ex-Dorothee Bos), 258 ft per most sources (238 ft per one), seized by U.S. Customs 1999 with over 10,000 lbs of cocaine aboard, sunk December 14, 2001 off Boynton Beach in about 80-118 ft. Goliath grouper site; spawning month differs by source.

Natural west-facing ledge off Boca Raton with an undercut more than 10 ft high, plus about 19-20 concrete Erojacks (some displaced by Hurricane David and later storms). Reported depth 40-82 ft depending on source. Reef/drift dive.

171-ft hopper barge sunk off Boca Inlet carrying concrete culverts (about 1,500-1,600 tons depending on source), donated as part of a fine on a dredging company. Flipped on sinking; rests upside down in about 50-70 ft.

194-ft freighter (Hamburg 1952, ex-Jacob Rusch; some sources say 197 ft) that grounded on a Palm Beach seawall on November 23, 1984 and was scuttled off Fort Lauderdale on March 30, 1985 in about 97 ft. Now broken and twisted after storms; entanglement hazard.

Former U.S. Coast Guard cutter Nemesis (WPC-111), 165 ft, launched July 7, 1934 (one list says 1933); WWII sub-chaser/escort; later a floating restaurant (dates differ by source); sunk June 9, 1991 off Deerfield Beach in about 70 ft. Goliath grouper reported in the wheelhouse.

Small steel tug A.L. Spencer (built 1940; 62-65 ft depending on source) that towed sand barges from the Bahamas; sunk as an artificial reef off Deerfield Beach (single-source date August 15, 1987) in about 65-70 ft, upright, bow south, near the Ancient Mariner.

215-ft Dutch freighter (launched 1956 as Nore; several later names) sunk May 12, 1990 off Pompano Beach for the Pompano Beach Fishing Rodeo's 25th anniversary. About 80-126 ft; shifted onto starboard side by storms (Irma 2017 per one source).

131-ft former oil-rig supply vessel seized by U.S. Customs for drug trafficking and sunk as an artificial reef off Fort Lauderdale (March 2, 1999 per one source; 1998 per another) in about 55-72 ft. Plaque honors dive instructor Ken Vitale; part of the Fort Lauderdale wreck trek.

Steel-and-concrete pyramids built from Radio Mambi broadcast tower sections and sunk in 1988 off Miami Beach, about 50 ft deep, about 20 ft tall each; reported as 19 pyramids by two sources and 15 by one county-list entry. Also called Ben's Antenna Reef.

Shallow reef around the Fowey Rocks Lighthouse (completed 1878) in Biscayne National Park, average depth about 15 ft, boat access only. The Arratoon Apcar was lost in 1878 a few hundred yards from the lighthouse construction site.

20-module 1000 Mermaids artificial reef deployed off Hollywood Beach on about October 31-November 1, 2022, in 35-40 ft of water about 1 mile offshore per the city (another source says a few miles southeast of Port Everglades); 5 of 20 modules are sculptures.
